HYPERSHIFT LARGE COMPANY RETRAINING
Stock Forecasting Model
Retraining Results
Current company lists with historical tests from 2022 to 2025
We completed 648 model training runs using the current NASDAQ-100 and the 100 largest
NYSE-listed companies. A model learns patterns from earlier prices to rank stocks by expected
returns. Coverage improved substantially. In 0 of the 4 main tests, the estimated uncertainty
range supported an advantage after trading costs over both SPY, a broad US market fund, and
QQQ, a NASDAQ-100 fund. All declared models are reported below.
These results describe a retrospective study of today’s large companies. Selecting companies
using their 2026 size or membership gives us information that would not have been available
in 2022. Better coverage makes the sample easier to explain, but does not remove that bias.

NYSE selection uses company market value, removes preferred-share rows and duplicate
companies, and uses Berkshire Class B. It includes foreign companies with NYSE-listed
depositary shares. This is a custom group of the largest NYSE-listed companies, separate from
the official NYSE 100 technology and growth index.

HYPERSHIFT LARGE COMPANY RETRAINING
How well forecasts ordered the stocks
A model tries to put stocks with higher future returns above stocks with lower future returns.
This chart shows its average agreement with the actual order over the following five trading
days. It includes every declared five-day neural model in both company groups.
Zero means no consistent agreement. Positive scores mean the model tended to put future
winners higher; negative scores mean it tended to reverse the order. The mathematical score
ranges from minus one to plus one. It is a rank correlation, called RankIC, rather than the
percentage of predictions that were correct.
Prediction quality and portfolio returns answer different questions. A portfolio holds only a
subset of stocks, while this score evaluates the entire eligible group. Position weights, price
variability and trading costs can change the investment outcome even when ordering scores
look similar.

HYPERSHIFT LARGE COMPANY RETRAINING
Study method and interpretation
Every annual test uses a fresh model trained on earlier prices. We used 16 trading days of input
and five measurements: daily price change, price relative to its five-day and twenty-day
averages, recent price variability, and trading activity. Models predict a price-change score
used to rank eligible stocks.
Test year Training signals Validation year
2022 2019 to 2020 2021
2023 2019 to 2021 2022
2024 2019 to 2022 2023
2025 2020 to 2023 2024
THINK is the original model family. A mixer combines patterns across stocks; the weaker
version reduces its influence. Huber reduces the influence of extreme forecast errors. Rank
variants add a training objective for ordering future winners above losers. These are local
adaptations, rather than official reproductions of the research papers.
We repeated each fit from three different starting weights, called seeds 7, 19 and 42.
Predictions from these runs are combined by their ranks; we do not choose the seed with the
best test return. Training makes at most thirty passes through the training data and stops after
six passes without improvement in validation forecast error. The optimizer is AdamW with
learning rate 0.001. Five-day models process batches of eight observations; daily models
process forty. All 648 declared fits finished.
Portfolio selection tests five weighting or retention methods and holdings of five, ten or twenty
stocks. It uses the median prior-validation half-year and seed Sharpe minus a variability
penalty. The architecture choice for an annual test uses that year’s and earlier validation
scores. The new five-day procedure also includes the three previously studied ranking-loss
variants; the earlier main procedure had sixteen models.
The sixteen cohort, horizon and year folds passed saved-split, training-only scaling, mature-
label and future-observation perturbation checks. Those checks support the chronology of the
saved-data pipeline. They do not certify historical membership, unrevised vendor data or an
independent confirmation test.

HYPERSHIFT LARGE COMPANY RETRAINING
Trading rules and research limits
A stock qualifies only with forty consecutive observed prices, finite model inputs and at least $1
million of average daily trading value over twenty sessions. A score produced at today’s close
trades at the next close. Each annual simulated account starts at $1 million. Normal orders are
capped at 1% of lagged average daily trading value; forced year-end liquidations may exceed
that cap. Per-side costs include a 2-basis-point commission, 5 basis points for spread and
slippage, and participation-based impact. A basis point is 0.01 percentage points. Cash earns
zero in the simulation, while Sharpe uses a fixed 3% annual hurdle. Days in this report mean
trading days.
The buy-recent-winners baseline also needs a finite six-month price-change measurement. It
excludes a newly listed stock until that history is available; the stock can still qualify for the
neural models earlier. This causal availability check was added after an error during validation,
before any new held-out performance metrics were computed.
Limits that remain
Current 2026 lists create future-universe selection and survivorship bias when applied to
2022–2025. The NASDAQ group is not a reconstruction of historical index membership, and the
NYSE group is not reselected by historical size. Company businesses can change through
restructurings. Price adjustments may include later revisions, and recent listings cannot
provide earlier histories. The test years were already examined during prior research. Any
apparent advantage remains conditional on this retrospective setup.
Before using the result as evidence of future trading performance, repeat the experiment with
membership and company-size information available at each historical decision date, plus a
genuinely new test period. The current report can support a presentation about exploratory
results on clearly defined large-company groups.
